desc:
Choose three indices i < j < k in nums. The value of the triplet is (nums[i] - nums[j]) * nums[k].

Return the maximum value over all triplets. If every triplet has a negative value, return 0.

Example: nums = [12, 6, 1, 2, 7] returns 77, from (12 - 1) * 7 with indices 0, 2, 4.
hints: Three nested loops are O(n<sup>3</sup>). Fix the middle index j: which i and which k are best for it?
All values are positive, so for a fixed j you want the largest nums[i] to the left of j and the largest nums[k] to the right of j (when the difference is positive).

Keep a running maximum of the values seen so far and a running best difference max(nums[i] - nums[j]). At each position, first try it as k (multiply the best difference by it), then update the difference, then update the maximum.
editorial: Every value is at least 1, so the best nums[k] for a given best difference is simply as large as possible and the best difference is as large as possible; the two choices do not interfere except through ordering (i < j < k).

Scan once, maintaining prefMax (the largest value before the current index) and bestDiff (the largest nums[i] - nums[j] over pairs i < j before the current index). At the current element x: first update the answer with bestDiff * x (x acts as k), then update bestDiff = max(bestDiff, prefMax - x) (x acts as j), then update prefMax = max(prefMax, x) (x acts as i). The order of those three lines guarantees the indices are strictly increasing.

Starting bestDiff at 0 is safe: it makes the product 0, which is the required answer when all triplets are negative. The largest possible result is below 9 * 108, so it fits in 32 bits. Time O(n), space O(1).
solution:
def maxTripletValue(nums):
    best = 0
    pref_max = 0
    best_diff = 0
    for x in nums:
        best = max(best, best_diff * x)
        best_diff = max(best_diff, pref_max - x)
        pref_max = max(pref_max, x)
    return best
